subject: ClearView pilot discovery — tech onboard sprint canvas
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@clearview.ai>, Aisha Khan <aisha.k@clearview.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 Jun 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: ClearView pilot discovery — tech onboard sprint canvas

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we kick off a short trial. Note: I attached a single-page success criteria doc to make acceptance simple.

High-level POC objective
- Validate Redwood inference in a streaming retrieval-augmented pipeline for ClearView's query assistant over financial data (latency and throughput targets, and end-to-end quality).

Proposed success criteria (draft)
- Latency: 95th percentile generate+stream <= 450ms for 512-token context (measured at Redwood edge in us-west).
- Throughput: sustain 30 concurrent sessions with <10% tail-slow events during a 1-hour window.
- Quality: match or exceed baseline F1 on the labeled test set (we'll use the 120-case prompt set you mentioned).
- Stability: no unhandled errors for 10k requests over the trial window.

Technical scope
- Integration: use Redwood Python SDK for streaming answers (streamed tokens + incremental tool-calls to your retrieval API). We can also run REST streaming if you prefer.
- Routes: generation (POST /v1/generate/stream), embeddings (POST /v1/embeddings), and optional rerank endpoint.
- Tool calling: we recommend the retrieval plugin pattern; Redwood can emit structured tool-call payloads you can safely validate.
- Data: session-level KV cache will be used; no customer PII will be stored in long-term caches unless you opt-in.

Timeline (proposed)
- Week 0 (alignment): finalize success criteria and owners (this week).
- Week 1 (kickoff + testbed): SDK handoff, sample snippets, and streaming smoke tests.
- Week 2 (integration sprint): run retrieval+inference integration, iterate on prompts.
- Week 3 (stress & regression): load tests, telemetry, and pre-acceptance checklist.
- Week 4 (acceptance): run acceptance tests and sign-off.

Owners (proposed)
- Redwood: Ben Carter (overall), Marissa Cole (SDK & handoff), Sergio Alvarez (runtime and streaming tests).
- ClearView: technical owner + one engineering lead (please confirm).

Ask from you
1) Confirm the two ClearView technical owners and a preferred pilot start week.
2) Confirm the success criteria bullets above or suggest edits — we can lock them into the acceptance doc.
3) Share minimal access: a short retrieval API sandbox URL and a couple sample documents for prompt tuning.

Attachments: clearview_pilot_success_criteria_v1.pdf (single-page acceptance + metrics), redwood_sdk_streaming_sample.py (snippet). Also linking a shared Drive canvas where we'll post the sprint checklist: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2Bcv_CLEARVIEW_PILOT

Thanks — I can set up the kickoff call once we have owners and a tentative start date.

—
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0138
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@clearview.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aisha Khan <aisha.k@clearview.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 Jun 2028 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ClearView pilot discovery — tech onboard sprint canvas

Ben — thanks for the clear recap. That looks good and I appreciate the concrete metrics. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Owners: I'll be the exec sponsor, Aisha Khan (aisha.k@clearview.ai) will be the engineering lead for integration, and Michael Lee (michael.lee@clearview.ai) will do the hands-on work. Please add them to the kickoff invite.
2) Compliance: we will need SOC2 Type II evidence and confirmation that Redwood supports customer-managed KMS for the pilot (or a plan for encrypted keys). Can you point us to where we can validate that?
3) Data residency: for now US-only; we expect logs to stay in us-west.

Start date: the team is available to start integration week of 2028-07-08. That gives us one week to finalize the MSA/DUA signatures.

Sample ask: can you provide the streaming SDK snippet and a tiny end-to-end sandbox that returns a mocked retrieval result so Michael can run an end-to-end local test? Also, on latency metric: if our baseline production call goes to an internal retrieval service, should we measure from Redwood edge to the client or include retrieval time? We prefer excluding internal retrieval latency in the initial SLO so we can isolate inference performance.

If you can share the SOC2 evidence and confirm the KMS approach, we'll sign the MSA and aim for 7/8 kickoff.

—
Daniel Park
Head of Product | ClearView Analytics
daniel.park@clearview.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 26 Jun 2028 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: ClearView sprint canvas — who owns what

Marissa / Sergio — following Daniel's notes below. They're aiming for a 2028-07-08 kickoff pending MSA and SOC2 checks. Draft assignments and an implementation canvas attached. Please review and flag anything missing.

Sprint breakdown (4-week trial):
- Week 0 (pre-kickoff, 3 days): legal/DUA sign, share Drive; Redwood to provide SDK snippet + mocked retrieval sandbox. Owner: Marissa (SDK) + Ben (coord).
- Week 1 (integration): SDK integration with their retrieval plugin. Verify token streaming and tool-call payloads. Owner: Marissa. Criteria: sample end-to-end run with mocked retrieval succeeds.
- Week 2 (integration validation): prompt tuning, prompt templates, caching rules, and incremental response checks. Owner: Marissa + ClearView eng.
- Week 3 (load & telemetry): run sustained load (30 concurrent sessions) and verify 95p latency. Sergio to run streaming stress harness and collect traces.
- Week 4 (acceptance): run the labeled test set, compile results, and produce acceptance report. Ben to coordinate sign-off.

Implementation to-dos (first 48hrs)
- Post SDK sample to Drive and a runnable mock sandbox (redwood_sdk_streaming_sample.py) — Marissa
- Prepare runtime config suggestions (batching, KV cache TTLs) and a default quantization suggestion — Sergio
- Create HubSpot plan and attach doc: HubSpot deal CV-2028-084 — Ben

Attachments: redwood_poc_onboard_canvas.xlsx (sprint canvas & task owner table). I'll drop telemetry dashboards into the Drive folder as soon as Sergio has the test harness output.

Let me know if owners want the kickoff calendar hold; I can propose 7/8 10am PT.

—
Ben
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@clearview.ai>, Aisha Khan <aisha.k@clearview.ai>, Michael Lee <michael.lee@clearview.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Jun 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ClearView pilot discovery — tech onboard sprint canvas

Daniel / Aisha / Michael — great, thanks for confirming owners and the tentative start week. Per your asks: 

- SOC2 & KMS: See SOC2 evidence (external link in Drive) and our KMS integrations note in the security appendix: we support customer-managed keys via standard KMS/HSM integrations in private deployments; for hosted pilots we can sign an encryption appendix and provide key separation controls. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2Bcv_CLEARVIEW_PILOT

- Streaming SDK sandbox: attached redwood_sdk_streaming_sample.py (runnable script that connects to a mocked retrieval endpoint). This is also in the Drive folder.

- Latency measurement: we agree to exclude ClearView's internal retrieval processing time from the initial inference SLO. We'll measure from Redwood edge (ingest) to first-streamed-token plus end-of-response. We'll capture spans so you can add retrieval time if needed.

Next steps and actions (we'll own these on our side):
1) Redwood to share kickoff invite for 2028-07-08 10:00 AM PT (calendar invite incoming).
2) ClearView to sign MSA/DUA (DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/to/msa/CV-2028-084).
3) ClearView to provision test retrieval sandbox and shared credentials (short-lived token).
4) Redwood to post SDK sample + mocked sandbox to Drive and run an initial smoke test before the call.

I've attached the single-page acceptance criteria (clearview_pilot_success_criteria_v1.pdf) and the sprint canvas spreadsheet (redwood_poc_onboard_canvas.xlsx). I'll also attach the SDK snippet directly to the HubSpot deal and the Drive folder for easy access.

Thanks — looking forward to kickoff.

—
